edition.en: Seven of the twenty passages of Gaozi I (book 6, part 1 of the Mencius), as given and numbered on Chinese Wikisource: 8, 9, 11, 13, 15, 19 and 20. Compared with the plain text of the Mencius in the Kanseki Repository and with Project Gutenberg eBook 24178; the online 茍 is corrected to 苟 four times.
edition.zh: 选《孟子·告子上》二十章中的七章，即维基文库编号的第八、九、十一、十三、十五、十九、二十章。与京都大学汉籍资料库（Kanseki Repository）所收《孟子》正文和古登堡计划电子书第 24178 号对校；维基文库误作“茍”的四处改为“苟”。

basis.en: A Warring States text; Mencius died about 289 BCE.
basis.zh: 战国文献，孟子约卒于公元前 289 年。

note.en: In this book Mencius argues that people are born with a good heart, and these seven passages are the ones about tending it: a mountain stripped of trees that would regrow if left alone, one day of sun against ten of frost, a chess pupil thinking about a swan. They are chosen for what they say about learning, which Mencius defines as going after the heart that has strayed. The last passage gives the craftsman’s standard: the full draw of the bow, the compass and the square.
note.zh: 孟子在这一篇里主张人生来就有善心，这里选的七章，讲的都是怎样养护它：一座被砍光的山，放着不管本会重新长出树来；晒一天，冻十天；学棋的人心里想着天鹅。选它们，是为了其中关于学习的话，孟子说学问之道无他，求其放心而已。最后一章给出了匠人的标准：拉满的弓，圆规和曲尺。

excerpt.orig: 故苟得其養，無物不長；苟失其養，無物不消。
excerpt.en: So, given its nourishment, there is nothing that will not grow; deprived of its nourishment, there is nothing that will not wither.
excerpt.zh: 故苟得其养，无物不长；苟失其养，无物不消。

gloss.en: Ox Mountain stood south-east of Linzi, the capital of Qi, the “great city” of the next sentence.
gloss.zh: 牛山在齐国都城临淄的东南，下句所说的“大国”即指临淄。

gloss.en: New shoots and the sprouts that come up from a cut stump.
gloss.zh: 新芽和从树桩上长出的嫩枝。

gloss.en: Bare and shining, stripped of growth.
The clear air of early dawn, before the day’s business begins: Mencius’s image for the heart when it has rested.
gloss.zh: 黎明时清明的气息，孟子用来比喻休息之后、尚未被白天的事务扰乱的心。

gloss.en: Fetter it and destroy it. 梏 is a wooden handcuff.
gloss.zh: 把它束缚、消灭掉。梏，木制的手铐，引申为束缚。

gloss.en: The night air: the good disposition that grows back in the stillness of night.
gloss.zh: 夜间滋生的清明之气，即在夜的宁静中重新生长出来的善心。

gloss.en: A saying attributed to Confucius and not found in the Analects.
Do not wonder at the king’s lack of wisdom. 或 is read as 惑, to be puzzled.
gloss.zh: 不要奇怪君王的不明智。或，同“惑”。

gloss.en: One day of sun, ten days of cold. 暴 is read as 曝, to expose to the sun; the phrase became the idiom 一暴十寒 for effort without persistence.
gloss.zh: 暴，同“曝”，晒。后来成为成语“一暴十寒”，比喻做事没有恒心。

gloss.en: Qiu the chess-player: the earliest named master of weiqi in Chinese records.
gloss.zh: 名叫秋的棋手，因善弈而称弈秋，是古书记载中最早的围棋名手。

gloss.en: Thinks of drawing his bow and shooting at it with a 繳, an arrow tied to a silk cord for bringing down birds.
gloss.zh: 想拿起弓箭去射它。缴，系在箭上的生丝绳，用来射鸟。

gloss.en: To seek the heart that has been let go, as one goes after a stray chicken or dog.
gloss.zh: 把放失的本心找回来罢了。放心，放失之心。

gloss.en: Paulownia and catalpa saplings as thick as can be held in two hands, or in one.
gloss.zh: 两手合围或一手握住那么粗的桐树、梓树。拱，两手合围；把，一手握住。

gloss.en: We are all equally human. 鈞 is read as 均.
The greater part is the heart that thinks; the lesser parts are the senses.
gloss.zh: 大体，指能思考的心；小体，指耳目等感官。

gloss.en: The function of the organ of the heart is to think; in early Chinese the heart, 心, is the seat of thought.
gloss.zh: 心这个器官的职能是思考。古人以心为思维器官。

gloss.en: Worse than wild millet and barnyard grass, weeds whose seeds can still be eaten.
gloss.zh: 还不如荑米和稗子。荑、稗都是似谷的杂草，结的籽也可以吃。

gloss.en: Yi was the legendary archer; 彀 is drawing the bow to its full extent.
gloss.zh: 羿，传说中善射的人；彀，把弓拉满。
